extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans, festival-goers, comedians and producers (especially in Los Angeles)
extracted.subtask_description: A short, journalistic listicle summarizing lessons learned from attending an alt-comedy festival (RIOT LA), highlighting what makes shows, lineups and festival experiences succeed or fail. Useful for attendees, performers and festival organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk-show/variety innovation and spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: "'Roustabout' was either the most fully realized one-off talk show spoof or Kurt Braunohler's bid at a gonzo series that needs to happen... Somewhere in between an episode of Pee-wee’s Playhouse and a Flaming Lips concert, 'Roustabout' managed to string together flying fruit, half-naked male dancers and jolly old St. Dick... with sit-down interviews and lie detector tests... The staggered, premature reveals throughout the night of 'the grandest finale' culminated in a heavy metal skeleton dance... and a marching band that led the crowd through Downtown to the after-party."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: originality, coherent one-off concept, willingness to mix theatrical/surreal spectacle with interview/comedy beats, and payoff through staged reveals and crowd interaction. Examples: unusual props/performers, genre-mixing, live-procession finales. Positive sign: show feels 'fully realized' and memorable; anti-pattern: spectacle without structure or payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticketing and access clarity (read the fine print)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Like the standard two-drink minimum at otherwise cheap stand-up shows, RIOT’s ticketing options came with a few caveats... pay-per-show tickets, which guaranteed admission, or a festival pass... we simply followed the fest’s suggestion to get in line at least 15 minutes before showtime... that didn’t prevent a pervasive anxiety in line as people wondered if popular shows would fill up. Perhaps that’s why some of the weekend’s most high-profile events required a separate ticket... for pass holders who wanted to see Comedy Bang! Bang! and the two KCRW storytelling showcases—three ticketed-only events—the total price of the weekend more than doubled."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: transparency of ticketing, clear communication about separate-ticket events, realistic capacity management, and fair value for pass holders. Guidance: advise arriving early, read event fine print, expect some high-profile events may be ticketed separately. Anti-patterns: surprise extra charges or pass holders being shut out of marquee shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local scene strength and talent diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: "RIOT’s lineup was a winner in large part due to LA’s own stellar comedy community... The weekend’s iTunes chart-topping podcasts feel like a victory lap from UCB favorites. From stand-up regulars to current comedians-in-residence—a special nod goes to the uproariously innovative Imaginary Radio Program with Drennon Davis—RIOT made a damn good case for the diversity and vitality of LA’s alt comedy scene."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: depth of local talent, cross-format representation (stand-up, sketch, podcasts), and presence of innovative local projects. Positive indicators: well-known local institutions represented, varied acts, and homegrown creative risk-taking. Use this to evaluate lineup strength and festival identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue concentration and local logistics (DTLA as hub)
rubrics_metrics.description: "As we walked between the fest’s five venues—all but one on the same stretch of sidewalk—and passed by the familiar faces of headlining comedians, Downtown felt like it was suddenly the place for comedy... there’s plenty of parking, public transit service and bars and apartment-dwellers within walking distance. And then the stench of urine hits you in the alleyway... you pass Third Street’s eye-opening encampment of tents. And then a very itchy homeless man manages to make his way to the stage..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: walkability and venue clustering, transit/parking convenience, nearby amenities, and how neighborhood conditions (cleanliness, safety, public nuisance) affect experience. Guidance: venue proximity can create a festival 'center' but external urban issues can intrude on shows and audience comfort; plan for crowd movement and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience behavior and festival community vibes
rubrics_metrics.description: "Maybe it was because of the comedy producers and struggling comedians that populated the crowd, but RIOT felt refreshingly polite and casual for a festival... Performers stood outside and chatted up fans... The Lot—a parking lot full of food trucks and arcade games—encapsulated everything that a festival should be. Attendees and performers alike mingled in a yard of positive vibes... Comedy nerds would point out comedians to friends and cross paths with their idols without even realizing..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: civility of audience, accessibility for networking, festival amenities that foster mingling (food trucks, games), and overall tone (polite vs raucous). Positive signs: performers approachable, constructive community energy; anti-patterns: hostile crowds, inaccessible VIP-only atmospheres that stifle community interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of live shows and the role of unpredictability
rubrics_metrics.description: "When Jon Benjamin took the stage... he and the show’s co-creator Leo Allen lambasted that the $30 event was, in fact, only worth $21... Nathan Fielder worked his way through the crowd to hand out envelopes stuffed with $9... then take back $2... a screening of the show’s hilarious pilot presentation and a table read... But all of that was upstaged when a homeless man managed to make his way to the front... Benjamin’s claim that this wasn’t a part of the show slowly began to penetrate. Cue some panicked staff, a generous bribe and a theater full of I’m-going-to-hell-for-this laughs at the man’s incomprehensible insistence that he doesn’t need money because he’s a sasquatch."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: ticket_price versus perceived comedic payoff, quality of curated content (screenings, table reads, guests), and how spontaneous/unplanned moments contribute to or detract from value. Guidance: audiences may accept high prices if content + memorable moments justify them; unpredictability can enhance comedy but requires good staff response and ethics (e.g., handling vulnerable individuals).
